html:
The Okanagan valley of British Columbia and Washington is the heart of the land of the Syilx, or Okanagan people, an Interior Salish nation; see Syilx for their wider territory.

The valley is a long chain of lakes, with Okanagan Lake at its centre, draining south into the Columbia. The Syilx fished for salmon, dug roots such as bitterroot, hunted deer in the hills and wintered in pit houses. From the 1810s fur traders used the valley as the route of their brigade trail north from the Columbia. After 1858 gold seekers and ranchers moved in, and from the 1890s fruit orchards filled the valley. The Syilx today live on reserves in Canada and on the Colville reservation in Washington. Their neighbours include the Nlaka'pamux.
